plan: Ten items from subskills not yet in the bank. 4 hard (rational inverse, empirical rule split at the mean, per-minute optimization, and the inverse trap) / 4 medium / 2 easy.

candidates.stem: If f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 3) for x ≠ 3, which of the following is f⁻¹(x) ?
candidates.explanation: Write y = (2x + 1)/(x − 3) and swap: x = (2y + 1)/(y − 3). Then xy − 3x = 2y + 1, so y(x − 2) = 3x + 1 and y = (3x + 1)/(x − 2).

A.rationale: This is the reciprocal 1/f(x), not the inverse.

B.rationale: This makes sign errors when collecting terms (−1 and +2).

C.rationale: This swaps the roles of the constants without solving for y.

hints: Swap x and y, then solve for y.
Collect the y terms on one side and factor out y.
candidates.remember: Inverse: swap x and y, then solve; the reciprocal is not the inverse.

author_checklist.hardness: solving for y requires collecting and factoring y; reciprocal trap

candidates.stem: The sum of three consecutive even integers is 8 more than twice the largest of the three. What is the smallest of the three integers?
candidates.explanation: Let the integers be n, n + 2, n + 4. Then 3n + 6 = 2(n + 4) + 8, so 3n + 6 = 2n + 16 and n = 10.

A.rationale: 8 sets the sum equal to twice the smallest plus 8.

hints: Name the integers n, n + 2, n + 4.
Translate "8 more than twice the largest."
candidates.remember: Consecutive even integers: n, n + 2, n + 4.

candidates.stem: In triangle ABC, the measure of angle A is 30°, the measure of angle B is 45°, and the side opposite angle A has length 10. What is the length of the side opposite angle B?
candidates.explanation: By the law of sines, b/sin 45° = 10/sin 30°, so b = 10 · (√2/2)/(1/2) = 10√2.

A.rationale: 5√2 multiplies by sin 45° instead of dividing by sin 30°.

B.rationale: 10 assumes the two sides are equal, as if the angles were equal.

D.rationale: 20 divides 10 by sin 30° but forgets to multiply by sin 45°.

hints: Which law relates sides to the sines of opposite angles?
candidates.remember: Law of sines: a/sin A = b/sin B.

candidates.subskill: Volume change when dimensions change unequally
candidates.stem: The radius of a right circular cylinder is halved and its height is doubled. The new volume is how many times the original volume?
candidates.explanation: V = πr²h. New volume = π(r/2)²(2h) = πr²h · (1/4)(2) = (1/2)πr²h.

A.rationale: 1/4 squares the radius change but ignores the doubled height.

C.rationale: 1 assumes halving and doubling cancel, forgetting that r is squared.

hints: Which dimension is squared in the volume formula?

strategy.explanation: Try r = 2, h = 1, then r = 1, h = 2.

candidates.remember: Squared dimensions change volume by the square of the factor.

candidates.stem: Test scores are approximately normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 8. Approximately what percent of scores are between 62 and 86?
candidates.explanation: 62 is 1 standard deviation below the mean and 86 is 2 above. From the mean down 1 SD is about 34%; up 2 SDs is about 47.5%. Total: about 81.5%.

C.rationale: 95% covers ±2 standard deviations, but the interval is not symmetric.

D.rationale: 97.5% is the percent below 2 standard deviations above the mean.

hints: How many standard deviations from 70 are 62 and 86?
candidates.remember: Split an asymmetric interval at the mean.

author_checklist.hardness: asymmetric interval requires splitting the empirical rule at the mean

candidates.stem: A poll of likely voters found that 52% support a ballot measure, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.A: It is plausible that fewer than half of all likely voters support the measure.
choices.B: A majority of all likely voters definitely supports the measure.
choices.C: Exactly 52% of all likely voters support the measure.
choices.D: Between 49% and 55% of the people polled support the measure.

candidates.explanation: The margin of error gives a plausible range of 49% to 55% for the whole population. Because the range includes values below 50%, a minority is plausible.

B.rationale: The plausible range dips below 50%, so a majority is not certain.

C.rationale: 52% is an estimate; the margin of error expresses uncertainty about it.

D.rationale: Exactly 52% of the people polled support it; the range describes the whole population.

hints: What range does a 3-point margin give?
Does that range include values under 50%?
candidates.remember: A margin of error describes the population, not the sample.

candidates.stem: What is the determinant of the matrix with first row 3, −2 and second row 4, 1 ?
candidates.explanation: For a matrix with rows (a, b) and (c, d), the determinant is ad − bc = (3)(1) − (−2)(4) = 3 + 8 = 11.

A.rationale: −11 computes bc − ad, reversing the order.

candidates.remember: Watch the sign when subtracting a negative product.

candidates.stem: A student estimated that a jar contained 250 marbles. The jar actually contained 200 marbles. What was the percent error of the estimate?

A.rationale: 12.5% divides the error by the sum, 400.

B.rationale: 20% divides the error by the estimate, 250, instead of the actual value.

D.rationale: 50% is the error in marbles, not a percent.

hints: What is the size of the error?
Divide by the actual value, not the estimate.
candidates.remember: Percent error divides by the actual value.

candidates.stem: A baker earns $2 profit on each muffin and $9 profit on each cake. Each muffin takes 5 minutes to make and each cake takes 40 minutes, and the baker has 480 minutes available. The baker must make at least 30 muffins. What is the greatest possible total profit?
candidates.explanation: Per minute, muffins earn $2/5 = $0.40 and cakes earn $9/40 = $0.225, so muffins are the better use of time. Making 96 muffins and no cakes uses all 480 minutes and earns $192, which is more than any mix that includes cakes.

A.rationale: $108 makes only cakes (12 of them) and ignores the 30-muffin minimum.

B.rationale: $132 makes the minimum 30 muffins and fills the rest with cakes, assuming the higher-profit item is better.

C.rationale: $150 splits the time evenly: 48 muffins and 6 cakes.

hints: Compare profit per minute, not profit per item.
Does the higher-profit item use time efficiently?
candidates.remember: When time is limited, compare profit per unit of time.

author_checklist.hardness: higher profit per item is the worse choice; must compare per-minute rates
